mu_name_from: ZzzOpenData.cpp: `AccessModel(MODEL_ALE, L"Data\\Item\\", L"Beer", 1)`, so MODEL_ALE is Beer01.bmd; OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser names group 14 number 9 the Ale.
why_this_one:
Lumen's first line, and the reason her window opened on an empty shelf: Market.Barmaid is two lines and neither was built, so Realm.Shelf served nothing. Drop level 15 with durability one - a single drink.

The asset is called Ale01 and not Beer01 because the world already has a Beer01: assets/world/lorencia/Beer01.json is the tavern's own barrel, and mu2.sh finds an asset by name across every folder, so a second Beer01 would shadow the first. The item field is the asset's name; the model it is cut from is Beer01.bmd, as sheet_from says.
profile_note: Not because a potion is a weapon but because the profile is about the art: a small painted sheet on a made object seen close, upscaled with the drawn model held back so a band of paint does not become a ridge. The Apple made the same argument. The default material is overridden per island below.

stats.note: OpenMU's row, copied rather than restated. Only the columns a drop and a shelf read are here - a potion has no damage roll, no stance and no hand, which is why it carries a Prize and no Arm. See shared/Rows.cs.
stats.call: Number = 9; Group = 14; DropsFromMonsters = true; DropLevel = 15; Durability = 1; Value = 30; Width = 1; Height = 2
stats.call_note: Written out as fields rather than as a call because that is what the source is: the potions are each built property by property, so the properties are quoted instead. See Potion01, the Apple, which set the shape.
stats.durability_note: One. A single drink, which is what Lumen sells it as.

sheet_from: Data/Item/bottle.ozt (32x32) from MuMain, which Beer01.bmd names bottle.tga. The same file was already in assets/textures for the tavern's Furniture01 and Furniture02 and Beer01 barrel, and decoded byte-identically here, which is a free check that the extraction is the same one.
sheet_note: A purple-brown bottle with a pale label. The alpha channel is present and cuts nothing - 0% under half - so it is not declared a cut-out; the sheet is solid glass with a paper label painted on, and the label is in the bottle's own island.
material_note: One island, the bottle and its label together, and it is a glass bottle: glass. The paper label ships with glass's roughness and its own paint, which at 32 pixels across is not a thing anybody can see.
